audience: A distance-focused road rider — sportive, club-run and all-day-endurance cyclist who wants a comfortable, efficient drop-bar bike with character, and who'd rather build their own one-of-a-kind frame than buy another anonymous carbon machine.

positioning.title: A road bike that stays smooth when the miles stack up.
positioning.lede: Built for endurance, not just the first 40km. Bamboo's natural vibration damping takes the sting out of rough tarmac and long days in the saddle, so you finish a century fresher — on a drop-bar frame you made with your own hands.

who_for.title: You ride long, not just fast
who_for.body: Sportives, club runs and all-day endurance miles. If finishing fresh matters more to you than a 200g weight saving, bamboo's damping earns its keep over the distance.

who_for.title: You want road comfort without a dead ride
who_for.body: Bamboo soaks up road buzz the way a good steel frame does, but stays torsionally stiff so your power still goes to the back wheel. Smooth, not flexy.

who_for.title: You'd rather build it than buy it
who_for.body: A frame nobody else owns, finished by you over a few weekends — and every kit funds a place on our prison frame-building course. Not for the watts-obsessed crit racer chasing the lightest aero rig.

faq.q: Is a bamboo road frame stiff and efficient enough for fast riding?
faq.a: Yes. Bamboo is torsionally stiff, so power transfer to the rear wheel is direct — builders ride theirs daily and on long tours. It's tuned for endurance comfort rather than crit-race rigidity, so you trade a little outright stiffness for a noticeably smoother ride over distance. Tensile strength is around 28,000 PSI, comparable to mild steel.

faq.q: How much does a finished bamboo road bike weigh?
faq.a: Bamboo is naturally a touch heavier than a top-end carbon race frame, so it's built for all-day comfort and durability rather than the lightest possible climbing weight. Most builders find the smoother ride and the fact they built it themselves more than worth it. Send us your build goals and we'll advise on the lightest sensible component spec.

faq.q: Will the frame survive years of big road miles?
faq.a: Yes. We've seen under a 1% failure rate across 4,000+ builds since 2012, the design has been independently tested with Swansea University, and frames last 8-12 years with proper care — many of our 2012 builds are still ridden daily. Seal it, dry it after wet rides and store it indoors.

faq.q: What drivetrain and groupset can I run?
faq.a: The frame works with all major road groupsets. Add one of our matched component packs — Shimano 105 hydraulic disc, a clean single-speed pack, or GRX for road-plus versatility — or source your own parts from any bike shop. We'll advise on the right setup for how you ride.

faq.q: How wide a tyre will it take?
faq.a: It's built around modern road rubber — comfortably running wider tyres than a classic race frame for lower pressures and more compliance on rough surfaces. Tell us the tyres you have in mind and we'll confirm clearance for your build before you order.
